The examination of the course consists of two parts: 

- a **self-reflection** (1-2 pages) following the seminar on Day 4
- a **group project** on multi omics data, with presentation on **24th October 2025**.


#### Details on the group project
The goal is for the students to perform omics data analysis using the methodologies presented in the course.

**Datasets**

During the first day of the course, we will present two multi-omics datasets. 
For each dataset, students can choose at least 3 omics and a research topic of interest.

**Groups**

The students will be divided into 4-5 groups, which will be communicated during the first week of the course. At least 2 groups will work on the same datasets, but might different omics.

**Presentations**

All presentations will be held on **24th October 2025**, via zoom (the link will be communicated during the course).
The presentations will be organized in sessions: each session will center around the same dataset (*e.g.*, two presentations per session).

**Key points:**

- Each presentation should last approximately 30 minutes, followed by 10 minutes of discussion (with primarily questions from the other group working on the same dataset). 
- You are expected to actively participate in the discussion of the other group working on the same dataset.
- Everybody should contribute to the preparation and presentation of their group's work.
- Suggested skeleton: brief background, explain which techniques you chose and why, present your results (figures or tables), conclusions, and limitations.
